data.outcome_summary: This OECD country notes report summarizes results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for Ireland, covering adults aged 16–65 assessed in 2022–23 across three domains: literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving. The assessment was administered exclusively on digital tablets and reports proficiency on 500-point scales with discrete proficiency levels; uncertainty is shown via 95% confidence intervals. Ireland’s mean performance is above the OECD average in literacy (263 points) but below in numeracy (260) and adaptive problem solving (249). The report also documents subgroup differences by age (lower proficiency among older adults), education attainment (large positive gradients with tertiary education), and immigrant background (native-born adults of native-born parents score higher in literacy). Finally, it links higher numeracy proficiency to better labour-force participation and higher wages, and it reports associations between high proficiency and life satisfaction/health, trust, and volunteering, while excluding doorstep-only respondents from several analyses to preserve comparability.
